title: Separated algebraic spaces of dimension at most one over a field are schemes
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum], separated and locally of finite type (the diagonal is a closed immersion and the morphism on etale scheme charts is locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Assume its topological Krull dimension is at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with the topology tested on an etale scheme atlas. Then $X$ is representable by a $K$-scheme. No quasi-compactness, properness, reducedness, or connectedness hypothesis is required; the empty space is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0ADD (lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus), applied at every point; a locally finite-type space over a field is locally Noetherian and dimension at most one bounds all local dimensions.

proof.text: First $X$ is locally Noetherian: every etale scheme chart $V\to X$ is locally of finite type over $K$ by the hypothesis. The field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $K$), so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes each such $V$ locally Noetherian. This is exactly the atlas definition of locally Noetherian for an algebraic space. Use [lem-a1-space-affine-atlas-open-cover] to cover $X$ by open subspaces $Z$ with surjective etale affine scheme atlases. Each $Z$ is quasi-compact by the last clause of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $X/K$, hence is closed and quasi-compact on scheme tests. Thus $Z$ is separated and Noetherian (locally Noetherian, quasi-compact, quasi-separated). Restriction of the locally Noetherian atlases to the open gives locally Noetherian atlases of $Z$ [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Tag 0ADD (lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus), first sentence: reduction to quasi-compact separated Noetherian open subspaces; Noetherian conventions are Tag 03EA

proof.text: For each open piece $Z$, its topological dimension is at most one: a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $|Z|$ gives a strict chain of their closures in $|X|$; intersection of these closures with $|Z|$ recovers the original chain. This proves the bound directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Fix $x\in|Z|$. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-finite-scheme-cover] to obtain a separated Noetherian $K$-scheme $U$ and a finite surjective $f:U\to Z$. By [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology], $f$ is locally quasi-finite. Hence [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-source-dimension-bound] gives $\dim|U|\leq\dim|Z|\leq1$. By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], every stalk $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ has dimension at most one. In particular the inequality holds at all points over $x$.

source.place: Tag 0ADD (lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus), first paragraph: finite cover and local dimension bound

proof.text: Put $R=U\times_ZU$. It is a scheme by diagonal representability [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The two projections $s,t$ are finite by base change [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology]. On test schemes an arrow is a pair $(a,b)$ with $f(a)=f(b)$; identity is $(a,a)$, inverse exchanges the pair, and composition sends $((a,b),(b,c))$ to $(a,c)$. These formulas define the groupoid laws [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] directly. The orbit of any chosen $u$ over $x$ is exactly $f^{-1}(x)$: one containment follows from $fs=ft$; for the other, any two points over $x$ lift to a point of $U\times_ZU$ by [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point]. This orbit is finite by [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-groupoid-codimension-one-invariant-affine] using step 2 to obtain an affine open $W\subseteq U$ containing the orbit with $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$.

source.place: Tag 0ADD (lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus), first paragraph and beginning of second paragraph: finite relation and invariant affine neighbourhood

proof.text: The open $W$ is saturated for $f$: if $w\in W$ and $v\in U$ have the same image, [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] gives a relation arrow between them, and invariance puts $v$ in $W$. Thus $f^{-1}(f(W))=W$. Since $f$ is surjective and closed [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology], the equality $|Z|\setminus f(W)=f(|U|\setminus W)$ shows that $f(W)$ is open. By the open-subspace correspondence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], let $Z^{\prime}\subseteq Z$ be the open subspace with this point set. Pulling back $Z^{\prime}$ to $U$ gives precisely $W$ (the same open-subspace correspondence). Consequently $W\to Z^{\prime}$ is the base change of $f$, and is finite [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology] and surjective. It contains $x$ in its image. The target $Z^{\prime}$ is locally Noetherian and separated by restriction; it is quasi-compact because it is the continuous surjective image of the affine scheme $W$. Hence $Z^{\prime}$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-finite-affine-descent] to conclude that $Z^{\prime}$ is an affine scheme.

source.place: Tag 0ADD (lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus), second paragraph: descend the saturated open and apply finite affine descent

proof.text: The construction gives representable open neighbourhoods of every point of every $Z$, hence a set-indexed cover of $X$ by representable opens (one can use the set of all open subsets that are representable). The fppf sheaf $X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] is in particular a Zariski sheaf. The inclusions of these open subfunctors are representable open immersions by their definition. For every scheme section $T\to X$, their pullbacks are open subschemes covering $T$: each point of $T$ maps to a point of $X$ in one of the opens, and pullback of that open has precisely the inverse-image point set [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. These verify all clauses of [lem-pc-schemes-criterion], which gives a representing scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}K$. If $X$ is empty, the empty family satisfies the same covering condition and the representing scheme is empty. No step imposed a global finite covering, reducedness, or connectedness.

lean.statement: theorem exists_scheme_of_separated_dim_le_one {K : Type u} [Field K] (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of K))) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 X.obj.obj) (𝟙 X.obj.obj))) (hlft : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of K))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (Point X.obj.obj) ≤ 1) : ∃ U : Over (Spec (.of K)), Nonempty (yoneda.obj U ≅ X.obj.obj)
lean.note: Separatedness is the closed-immersion scheme-test condition for the diagonal in presheaves on Over (Spec K); local finite type is tested on every etale scheme chart. Reuses the landed Point and pointTopologicalSpace; their existing definition node is added to stmt_deps. The conclusion is a representing scheme over K, expressed by an isomorphism of presheaves on Over (Spec K).
